turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung was dead set on doing as O-lan said, he would give their son to the maid to care for, and she would be his wife. But how could O-lan be so sure that she would be a good wife to him?
turns.speech: I will do as you say, O-lan. I will give our son to the maid to care for, and she will be his wife. But how can you be so sure that she will be a good wife to him?

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid didn't think she could be a good wife to Wang Lung's son, she was just a young woman, not even a year married yet.
turns.speech: I-I don't think I could be a good wife to your son, sir. I'm just a young woman, not even a year married yet.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung spoke sternly, What does it matter if she is young or not a year married? She has been trained by his wife, and she knows how to manage a household.
turns.speech: What does it matter if you are young or not a year married? You have been trained by my wife, and you know how to manage a household.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung spoke to O-lan, telling her that she was a good girl, and that she would learn to manage the household as well as she had. He would not have her worrying about being young or inexperienced, for she would be his son's wife and take care of him.
turns.speech: You are a good girl, and you will learn to manage the household as well as O-lan has. I will not have you worrying about being young or inexperienced, you will be my son's wife and you will take care of him.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan was tired, but she was at peace knowing that her son would be taken care of. She had seen many winters come and go, and she knew that it was time for her to rest.
turns.speech: I am tired, Wang Lung, but I am at peace knowing that my son will be taken care of. I have seen many winters come and go, and I know that it is time for me to rest.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung would not have O-lan worrying about her mother's rest, child. She would be at peace, knowing that her son would be well taken care of.
turns.speech: I will not have you worrying about your mother's rest, child. She will be at peace, knowing that her son will be well taken care of.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan must see Wang Lung married and settled before she goes.
turns.speech: I must see him married and settled before I go

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung was well, for he had their son and their farm to care for.
turns.speech: Do not worry about me, my wife. I will be well, for I have our son and our farm to care for.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He would take care of Father, and the farm, and he would be married soon, just as O-lan wanted.
turns.speech: Mother, I will take care of Father, and the farm, and I will be married soon, just as you want.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung spoke softly, his eyes fixed on the eldest son, Do not speak of marriage and settlement now, child. His mother needs rest, and he needs to care for her, not think of his own future.
turns.speech: Do not speak of marriage and settlement now, child. Your mother needs rest, and I need to care for her, not think of my own future.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He spoke softly, his words a gentle reassurance, as he said, Don't worry, Mother, he would take care of Father and the farm, and he would be married soon. It would be just like she wanted.
turns.speech: Don't worry, Mother, I'll take care of Father and the farm, and I'll be married soon. It will be just like you want.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan was tired, she had been working all day, but she wanted to see the marriage preparations begin, it would bring her peace to know their son was settled.
turns.speech: I will rest now, but I want to see the marriage preparations begin. It will bring me peace to know our son is settled.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan to remain silent, assuring her that he would take care of everything, just as she had always done for him and their son.
turns.speech: O-lan, do not speak of this now, you must rest and I will take care of everything, just as you have always done for me and our son

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He would take care of everything, Mother, just as Father was taking care of her. He would see to it that the marriage preparations began soon, so she could rest easy.
turns.speech: I will take care of everything, Mother, just as Father is taking care of you. I will see to it that the marriage preparations begin soon, so you can rest easy.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan's eyes narrowed, her voice firm, as she said, She must see it done, child. She must know their son is settled before she goes.
turns.speech: I must see it done, child. I must know our son is settled before I go.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid should go and start preparing for the marriage ceremonies, if it would bring O-lan peace, Mother.
turns.speech: I should go and start preparing for the marriage ceremonies, if it would bring you peace, Mother.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He would go with O-lan to start preparing for the marriage ceremonies, it would bring her peace to know that everything was being taken care of.
turns.speech: I will go with the maid to start preparing for the marriage ceremonies, Mother. It will bring you peace to know that everything is being taken care of.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid was eager, she said, to help with the preparations for the wedding, and she would go, Mother, to start making the arrangements, so it would be a beautiful one for the son and his bride.
turns.speech: I will go, Mother, and start making the arrangements for the wedding. May I also help with the preparations for the ceremony, so it will be a beautiful one for the son and his bride?

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan thought it would be good to have a small celebration before she went, to bring her joy and peace.
turns.speech: It would be good, I think, to have a small celebration before she goes, to bring her joy and peace.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung knew it was hard for O-lan to think of this now, but he would not have her burdened with worry. He would see to it that the marriage was arranged and the ceremonies were done as she wished.
turns.speech: O-lan, I know it is hard for you to think of this now, but I will not have you burdened with worry. I will see to it that the marriage is arranged and the ceremonies are done as you wish.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
